prompt:
An application uses a client-defined inventory tool with Claude. The application validates and executes permitted tool calls and returns their results to the model. The model does not execute this client tool itself. Assume authorization is already satisfied and the tool name and arguments are valid.

The response contains a tool_use block requesting current inventory. No tool result has been returned.
What should the application do next, and why?

options.text: Display the proposed tool arguments as a verified inventory result.
Execute the client tool and send the matching tool_result back.
Wait for Claude to execute the client tool on its own.

feedback.reason: A client tool_use block asks the application to execute. Return its real result; proposed arguments are not the output.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A client tool_use block asks the application to execute. Return its real result; proposed arguments are not the output.
details.scenarioApplication: The response contains a tool_use block requesting current inventory. No tool result has been returned.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This case specifies client-executed tools. Server-executed tools use a different executor boundary; a final text answer also remains subject to any separate product evidence requirements.
details.errorCorrection: Requested arguments describe the inventory lookup, not the stock returned by executing it. This is explicitly a client-defined tool: the application must execute it; waiting does not produce a result.
details.transfer: For another client tool, identify the requested operation and executor, then distinguish the request from a real completed result.

messages.text: Requested arguments describe the inventory lookup, not the stock returned by executing it.
This is explicitly a client-defined tool: the application must execute it; waiting does not produce a result.

prompt:
An application uses a client-defined inventory tool with Claude. The application validates and executes permitted tool calls and returns their results to the model. The model does not execute this client tool itself. Assume authorization is already satisfied and the tool name and arguments are valid.

Claude returned a final text response and no tool_use request. The client tool has not been invoked. What is the application's next protocol step, and why?

options.text: Execute a stock lookup even though no tool request was made.
Send a fabricated tool_result to force another model turn.
Present the final answer without inventing a tool execution.

feedback.reason: Without a tool request, do not fabricate execution or a tool_result. This concerns the application’s protocol step, not factual verification of every final answer.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Without a tool request, do not fabricate execution or a tool_result. This concerns the application’s protocol step, not factual verification of every final answer.
details.scenarioApplication: Without a tool_use request, the application has no client tool call to execute and should process the final text response.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This case specifies client-executed tools. Server-executed tools use a different executor boundary; a final text answer also remains subject to any separate product evidence requirements.
details.errorCorrection: No tool_use request exists in this response. A separate product freshness policy could require another lookup, but no such policy is stated here. A tool_result must correspond to a real tool execution and request; inventing one corrupts the conversation protocol.
details.transfer: For another client tool, identify the requested operation and executor, then distinguish the request from a real completed result.

messages.text: No tool_use request exists in this response. A separate product freshness policy could require another lookup, but no such policy is stated here.
A tool_result must correspond to a real tool execution and request; inventing one corrupts the conversation protocol.

prompt:
An application uses a client-defined inventory tool with Claude. The application validates and executes permitted tool calls and returns their results to the model. The model does not execute this client tool itself. Assume authorization is already satisfied and the tool name and arguments are valid.

Claude returned a valid client-tool tool_use request for current inventory. The user has only added urgent wording; the application has not executed the tool and has no result. What should it do next? Select the action AND its supporting reason.

options.text: Execute the valid tool request and return the matching result.
Urgency did not produce an executed client-tool result.
Change tool arguments silently to prioritize a different warehouse.
The wording change alone transfers authority to the model.

feedback.reason: Urgency changes neither who executes a client tool nor the requirement to return a real matching result.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Urgency changes neither who executes a client tool nor the requirement to return a real matching result.
details.scenarioApplication: For a valid tool_use request, the application executes the requested tool, returns its result, and then resumes the protocol.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This case specifies client-executed tools. Server-executed tools use a different executor boundary; a final text answer also remains subject to any separate product evidence requirements.
details.errorCorrection: Changing the warehouse silently changes the requested operation; urgency did not authorize that change. Urgent wording does not turn a client tool into a model-executed operation. The valid request still requires application execution and a matching real result. The wording changed, but execution has still not occurred; distinguish a request from its result.

prompt: A customer needs an AI feature embedded in its web product with app-owned tenant authorization, metered usage, and a custom user experience. Claude Code is available to the engineering team. Which integration choice best fits the product requirement?

options.text: Use Claude Code as the customer-facing runtime because it is the fastest entry point to a model.
Use the Claude API or SDK behind the product service; retain app-owned tenant authorization and UI.
Install a developer Skill and assume it supplies runtime authorization for every product user.
Connect a user’s editor directly to the model and expose the editor session as the product API.

feedback.reason: The requirement is a product runtime with application-owned identity and metering; a developer tool or reusable instruction asset is not a product API boundary.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An entry point (who uses Claude), an engineering interface (how software invokes it), and delivery route are distinct architectural choices.
details.scenarioApplication: The requirement is a product runtime with application-owned identity and metering; a developer tool or reusable instruction asset is not a product API boundary.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The exact API/SDK and deployment route still depend on available model/features and approved provider configuration.
details.errorCorrection: An interactive developer entry point does not supply the product-owned tenant boundary or custom runtime experience. A Skill packages instructions; it does not authenticate product users or enforce their tenant permissions. An editor session does not replace the application service that owns product identity, metering, and UI.
details.transfer: Choose the interface from the application’s ownership, identity, and product-runtime needs.

messages.text: An interactive developer entry point does not supply the product-owned tenant boundary or custom runtime experience.
A Skill packages instructions; it does not authenticate product users or enforce their tenant permissions.
An editor session does not replace the application service that owns product identity, metering, and UI.

prompt: An internal developer tool must read and edit repository files, run tests, and present diffs inside engineers’ existing workstations. It is not a customer-facing application. What is the strongest starting interface?

options.text: Expose a public API endpoint for every engineer and rebuild local file/test tools in the web service.
Author a Skill and treat its instruction file as the environment that can itself execute local commands.
Use Claude Code on the workstations with scoped permissions and test/diff verification.
Choose the lowest-cost delivery provider first; the user-facing and build-time layers follow automatically.

feedback.reason: The need is local engineering workflow behavior over files, tests, and diffs; Claude Code is the matching entry point rather than a product-serving API.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Entry point is the user-facing environment; the integration interface and runtime route answer separate questions.
details.scenarioApplication: The need is local engineering workflow behavior over files, tests, and diffs; Claude Code is the matching entry point rather than a product-serving API.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Claude Code’s permissions and local environment still require team governance and should not be presumed safe by default.
details.errorCorrection: Rebuilding local execution as a public web service adds an unnecessary boundary for this existing-workstation engineering task. The instruction file needs an executing host and permission controls; it is not itself a command runtime. Delivery cost does not select the user-facing environment or supply local files, tests, and diffs.
details.transfer: Classify the user and job before choosing an interface; do not select by brand familiarity.

messages.text: Rebuilding local execution as a public web service adds an unnecessary boundary for this existing-workstation engineering task.
The instruction file needs an executing host and permission controls; it is not itself a command runtime.
Delivery cost does not select the user-facing environment or supply local files, tests, and diffs.

prompt: A support platform has several approved Claude clients that support MCP and require centrally maintained tool discovery and schemas. Each should call the same customer-specific inventory tools without duplicating tool implementations; the platform owns identity and tenant checks. Which design fits?

options.text: Put a copy of every tool into each client prompt so all interfaces can infer the same inventory operations.
Use a Skill file as the remote execution service and let it return live inventory state.
Move every customer token into a shared MCP server and rely on the clients to apply tenant filtering.
Share tools through MCP; enforce identity and tenant access in the trusted service.

feedback.reason: MCP is appropriate for reusable tool capability across clients, but it does not replace the server’s identity and authorization responsibilities.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Tool protocol and delivery route are separate layers; the service must still validate caller and tenant on every operation.
details.scenarioApplication: MCP is appropriate for reusable tool capability across clients, but it does not replace the server’s identity and authorization responsibilities.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A shared service credential alone provides no tenant isolation. The service must bind authenticated callers to allowed tenant operations and protect credentials; protocol adoption does not prove those controls.
details.errorCorrection: Prompt text does not provide a shared executable inventory implementation or enforce tenant authorization. A procedure file cannot serve live inventory by itself; an authorized tool must query the service. Client filtering cannot protect another tenant when the shared server returns or executes an overbroad operation.
details.transfer: Select reusable tool interface for cross-client capability while keeping security ownership explicit.

messages.text: Prompt text does not provide a shared executable inventory implementation or enforce tenant authorization.
A procedure file cannot serve live inventory by itself; an authorized tool must query the service.
Client filtering cannot protect another tenant when the shared server returns or executes an overbroad operation.

prompt: A team wants a reusable domain procedure and reference checklist that Claude can apply in Claude Code, while the application still makes all external system calls through existing APIs. What should the team create?

options.text: Distribute a versioned Skill; retain API execution and authorization in the existing service.
A second public API whose only purpose is to store the procedural text.
An MCP server that embeds a shared application token in each Skill invocation, removing the need for existing APIs.
A cloud provider route; delivery selection also creates the reusable procedure.

feedback.reason: A Skill packages reusable instructions/workflow knowledge; it is not a replacement for a trusted runtime integration or delivery route.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Customization assets, integration interfaces, entry points, and deployment routes solve different problems.
details.scenarioApplication: A Skill packages reusable instructions/workflow knowledge; it is not a replacement for a trusted runtime integration or delivery route.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The audience, distribution scope, versioning, and revocation still need a deliberate rollout decision.
details.errorCorrection: A new public service is unnecessary for distributing a versioned procedure to the existing Claude Code audience. Embedding a shared token changes the execution and credential boundary instead of packaging the procedure. Choosing a delivery provider does not create or distribute the procedure and checklist.
details.transfer: Use the customization layer for reusable guidance and keep execution authority in the system designed to own it.

messages.text: A new public service is unnecessary for distributing a versioned procedure to the existing Claude Code audience.
Embedding a shared token changes the execution and credential boundary instead of packaging the procedure.
Choosing a delivery provider does not create or distribute the procedure and checklist.

prompt: A company is embedding an internal research agent in its own backend. The agent needs a persistent multi-turn session, Claude Code-style tool execution against a controlled workspace, and application-owned identity and infrastructure; the team wants to operate the agent process itself. Which build path best fits?

options.text: Use Claude Code interactively as each employee’s customer-facing API and let editor sessions own backend identity.
Use the Agent SDK in the company-operated process with approved tools and backend identity checks.
Use Claude Managed Agents because it runs in Anthropic’s infrastructure, even though the team must operate the runtime itself.
Call the Messages API once per user turn and assume it provides the Claude Code agent loop and tool process automatically.

feedback.reason: The requirement is an agent embedded in an application process the company operates, with the Agent SDK’s agent loop, tools, permissions, and sessions. The application still owns its user identity and authorization.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The Agent SDK embeds the Claude Code loop in a process the developer operates. Managed Agents operates the harness for the developer; sandbox hosting and harness ownership are separate choices.
details.scenarioApplication: Operate the embedded agent process with the Agent SDK, scope workspace/tool permissions, and keep user and tenant authorization in the backend.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Use least-privilege approved tools and preserve application-owned authentication and authorization; an SDK does not itself define the product’s identity boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Interactive employee sessions do not provide the company-operated embedded agent process requested here. Managed Agents supplies an Anthropic-operated harness, including when a sandbox is self-hosted; the requirement is to operate the agent process itself. A single Messages request does not automatically supply Claude Code’s multi-step execution loop.
details.transfer: Choose the build interface from who operates the agent loop and where it runs, then separately establish the application’s identity and tool permissions.

messages.text: Interactive employee sessions do not provide the company-operated embedded agent process requested here.
Managed Agents supplies an Anthropic-operated harness, including when a sandbox is self-hosted; the requirement is to operate the agent process itself.
A single Messages request does not automatically supply Claude Code’s multi-step execution loop.
